# Dashboard Requirements Quality Checklist: Execution Dashboard

**Purpose**: Review the completeness, clarity, consistency, and measurable quality of Feature 007 dashboard requirements
**Created**: 2026-09-29
**Feature**: [Execution Dashboard specification](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are all dashboard header fields, including optional lifecycle timestamps and duration, explicitly identified? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK002 Are all five supported execution statuses and their accessible, non-color-only presentation requirements covered? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK003 Are the four persisted counters distinguished from repository and finding detail availability? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK004 Are historical configuration name, GitLab URL, selected groups, and selected repositories all required from the captured snapshot? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK005 Are Overview, Repositories, Findings, and Details responsibilities clear enough to avoid missing or redundant information? [Completeness, Spec §FR-009]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK006 Is the meaning of “duration when calculable” precise for pending, running, final, and missing-timestamp cases? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK007 Is it clear that the completion message comes from the execution API and means orchestration completed without repository mining? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK008 Do unavailable repository/finding details clearly mean detail records are absent, while a zero counter remains valid persisted data? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK009 Is “safe error information” bounded to a safe code and summary, with all prohibited internal details identified? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK010 Is the fallback history destination for direct dashboard entry defined when no history context is available? [Clarity, Spec §FR-012]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK011 Do snapshot requirements consistently prohibit replacing historical values with current Monitoring Configuration state? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002, Spec §FR-008, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK012 Are the separate group and repository scope categories consistent with the prohibition on group expansion or GitLab lookups? [Consistency, Spec §FR-007, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK013 Are requirements consistent that absent timestamp values are not fabricated while completed executions show duration only when available? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK014 Are successful orchestration, zero mining counters, and unavailable repository/finding details described without implying repositories were analyzed? [Consistency, Spec §FR-005, Spec §FR-006, Spec §FR-009]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK015 Can each success criterion be evaluated objectively from specified displayed values, navigation outcomes, or defined accessibility/responsive standards? [Measurability, Spec §Success Criteria]
- [ ] CHK016 Are “understandable recovery paths” and normalized error feedback defined with enough user-facing criteria to assess consistently? [Measurability, Spec §SC-007, Spec §FR-013]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK017 Are primary entry and return journeys covered for both global history and configuration-specific history, as well as direct entry? [Coverage, Spec §FR-001, Spec §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK018 Are loading, not-found, retrieval failure, retry, and refresh requirements defined as distinct states and recovery paths? [Coverage, Spec §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK019 Are all lifecycle statuses addressed, including partially completed executions without repository-level detail? [Coverage, Spec §FR-004, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK020 Are historical scope empty states and safe error cases covered without inventing data or exposing implementation internals? [Coverage, Spec §FR-007, Spec §FR-010, Edge Cases]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK021 Are empty group and repository selections distinguished from unavailable scope metadata? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-007, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK022 Are long execution identifiers, GitLab paths, and scope labels covered by readable responsive behavior without losing their meaning? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-015, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK023 Is behavior defined when a running record lacks a calculable duration, without requiring a live timer? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-003, Edge Cases]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK024 Are keyboard operation, tab semantics, focus order, loading/error announcements, and accessible metric labels covered across dashboard sections? [Accessibility, Spec §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK025 Are the representative viewport sizes and no-page-overflow outcome specified clearly enough to assess responsive usability? [Coverage, Spec §FR-015, Spec §SC-009]
- [ ] CHK026 Are data safety and privacy requirements explicit for credentials, stack traces, provider bodies, database details, and internal execution metadata? [Security, Spec §FR-010, Spec §FR-016]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK027 Is the Feature 006 detail response identified as the authoritative source for every displayed execution, snapshot, counter, completion, and error value? [Dependency, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK028 Is the conditional nature of any detail-contract extension clear, including the restriction to already-persisted safe data? [Dependency, Spec §FR-016, Scope Boundaries]
- [ ] CHK029 Are repository processing and findings generation clearly deferred so unavailable states cannot be mistaken for delivered capabilities? [Scope, Spec §FR-017, Scope Boundaries]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [ ] CHK030 Do the requirements avoid implying that a zero persisted count means detail data is unavailable or that completion means mining succeeded? [Conflict, Spec §FR-005, Spec §FR-006, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK031 Are the terms “empty,” “unavailable,” and “not yet available” used consistently for zero counters versus absent detail records? [Terminology, Spec §FR-005, Spec §FR-009]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`.
- Items evaluate specification quality and traceability; they are not implementation test cases.
- Add comments or findings inline.
- Link to relevant resources or documentation.
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference.
